rationale: The buyer is a named, budget-holding professional — Salesforce developers and admins at companies or ISVs already paying $300–$1,500+/user/year for Gearset/Copado — and Agentforce deployment friction is a documented, unsolved pain point in the ecosystem right now, giving strong willingness-to-pay signals. The total of 6.4 clears the build threshold, but operational_autonomy sits at 6, just below the required floor of 7: a deployment validator can partially automate (Claude reads metadata, surfaces errors, proposes fixes), but the remediation steps — configuring CMS workspaces, adjusting org permissions, pushing corrected packages — still require human action in the Salesforce org, making this closer to a guided-troubleshooting tool than a fully hands-off service. Validate first to confirm that a report-and-recommend model (no hands-on org access needed) achieves sufficient customer value autonomously.
solution_plan: The service is an Agentforce Cross-Org Deployment Validator: a user pastes their deployment error log and metadata XML into a web form, and Claude analyses it against known Agentforce deployment constraints (CMS workspace permissions, org feature flags, metadata dependencies), then returns a plain-English diagnosis and a step-by-step remediation checklist — delivered instantly in the browser and via email. Build: the factory builds a Claude prompt chain trained on Salesforce deployment error patterns, a simple landing page with a Stripe payment link ($49 one-time report or $79/mo for unlimited), and a text/file intake form; no coding by Youval. Sell: reach Salesforce developers via Salesforce Stack Exchange answers, the Trailblazer Community, and targeted LinkedIn outreach to Salesforce admins/devs at ISV companies; every outreach batch requires Youval's approval before sending. Maintain: form submission triggers Claude analysis and automated email delivery; billing is Stripe self-serve; the only recurring human step is approving outreach and monitoring for edge-case errors that need prompt refinement. Realistic ceiling: this works well as a diagnostic tool but customers will quickly want it to also push fixes — that requires Salesforce API integration and per-org credentials, which significantly raises complexity; set that expectation before building.
notes: build_gate failure: operational_autonomy=6 (floor 7). If the product scope is limited to diagnosis + checklist (no automated fix push into the org), autonomy could plausibly reach 7 — validate this assumption with 3-5 paying customers before committing to build.
